title: HW grid marginal-cost probe and regression sentinel for token p95 & throughput
creator: Ava Patel
description: Objective: Build a reproducible probe that computes marginal cost-per-token and stable p95 throughput estimates across our HW matrix (A10, L4, A100, H100). The probe should operate as a long-running harness and a lightweight sentinel for regressions (automated alerts) that integrates into Console dashboards and runtime alerting. This ticket scopes the initial probe implementation, analysis heuristics, and short-term alert policy. We intentionally focus on marginal (delta) cost per token and p95 latency/throughput since those drive customer SLOs and unit economics.
steps: Design canonical workload: 60/30/10 split of short/medium/long prompts with synthetic prefix lengths to exercise KV cache warm/cold behavior.

Implement run harness: containerized job in infra/benchmarks repo that spins up VMs on each target GPU class, runs steady-state and tail workloads, collects per-request tokens/sec, latency histogram, cost meter (USD normalized), and GPU telemetry (util, power, memory).
Add marginal-cost calculation: compute cost-per-token as (cost_of_run - baseline_idle_cost) / total_tokens, with per-batch attribution for mixed-precision and quantized kernels.

Instrument p95/EWMA + CUSUM regression detector: maintain running EWMA of p95 and tokens/sec with configurable lookback windows; enable CUSUM to detect sustained positive deviations beyond dynamic thresholds.

Produce dashboard metrics and a compact alert payload for Console: include run_id, hw_type, model_variant, batch_distribution, kv_cache_state, samples, median_cost, p95_latency, tokens_per_sec_p95, and estimated margin delta.
Run initial sweep across A10/L4/A100/H100 for two model variants (open-70b-q4, opt-13b-fp16) in both warm and cold KV cache modes.
Publish results and recommended cost knobs (batching, quantization profile, target concurrency) into a new Console recipe and a short PRD for Optimize team.

Ship a lightweight alert rule in Console that triggers a PagerDuty policy when marginal_cost_per_token increases >10% for 3 consecutive windows and p95 latency regresses >15% with >5000 sample tokens in the window.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run end-to-end on A10/L4/A100/H100 and emit a stable JSON summary containing cost_per_token, p95_latency, tokens_per_sec_p95, and run metadata.
Regression detector flags synthetic regressions in unit tests (simulated drift) with <=1 false negative in 50 synthetic runs.
Console dashboard tile renders marginal_cost_per_token and p95 trend per HW row and links back to raw run artifacts.
Run reproducibility: rerunning same harness within 24 hours yields cost_per_token within 5% and p95 within 10% for steady-state workloads (given similar spot prices).
test_plan: Unit tests for cost model: validate attribution logic, spot/ondemand normalization, and bootstrap CI for median cost.
Regression detector tests: synthetic injection harness that adds controlled latency noise and cost shifts to validate EWMA + CUSUM parameters.
Integration runs: 3 full sweep jobs (warm/cold/steady-state) per HW type, each producing >= 2000 token samples per bucket.
A/B run for batching knob: compare baseline batching policy vs recommended policy to measure delta cost-per-token and p95 impact.
Stability runs across price volatility: run same config at two different spot price points to ensure cost model normalizes correctly.
results_summary: (placeholder) Initial validation sweep executed on 2026-03-05: A100 and H100 show expected lower marginal cost-per-token for long sequences; L4 shows best small-batch latency for short prompts but higher cost for long sequences. Observed noise in A10 runs due to spot eviction churn; plan to add a short-term smoothing window and record spot metadata per-run. Detailed CSV artifacts linked below.
